page: Amazon Web Services c8i.12xlarge is a compute-optimized instance based on the AWS Nitro hypervisor architecture. It is equipped with dedicated Intel Xeon 6975P-C processors offering 24 physical cores and 48 virtual CPUs running at a clock speed of 3.9 GHz. The memory subsystem consists of 96.0 GB of DDR5 RAM clocked at 7 GHz, maintaining a 1:2 compute-optimized memory-to-core ratio of 2.0 GB per vCPU. The processor configuration incorporates 48 KB of L1 data cache, 2 MB of L2 cache, and a large 480 MB shared L3 cache. Instruction set extensions include AVX-512, Intel AMX for tile and INT8 execution, and AVX-VNNI.

The c8i.12xlarge instance does not bundle local NVMe or SSD storage, requiring persistent workloads to utilize network-attached storage volumes. Network connectivity is delivered through the Nitro subsystem, providing a baseline network bandwidth of 22 Gbps. The instance provides zero complimentary public IPv4 addresses, utilizing private VPC network addressing by default. There are no discrete hardware accelerators or GPUs included on this instance type.

Benchmark evaluations reflect strong execution across compute and memory-intensive operations. The instance achieved top-tier scores in Geekbench text processing (2,856.0) and image processing (20,815.0), alongside 52,615.0 points in Clang compilation. Small-model LLM text generation reached 337.55 tokens per second, aided by AMX matrix acceleration and DDR5 memory bandwidth reaching 195.86 GB/s on large uncached read blocks. High-throughput operations yielded 88.09 million operations per second on Redis SET tests and 81.79 GB/s in static web serving. Given its compute density and lack of local storage, the instance fits compute-bound applications, CI/CD compilation pipelines, batch processing, web serving fleets, and CPU-based machine learning inference.
